newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey to tender part of Iran gas pipeline next week.
newsitem.headline: Turkey to tender part of Iran gas pipeline next week.

text.p: Turkey will announce a tender next week to build the first part of a pipeline to carry Iranian natural gas under a project to cost about $1 billion in total when completed, Energy Minister Recai Kutan said on Monday.
"Bids for the tender for engineering and construction of the pipeline section from the Iranian border to Erzurum province will be invited next week," Kutan told reporters.
Officials said the pipeline section, to cost around $200 million, is about 250 km (155 miles) long.
"The announcement will be made in national newspapers," Kutan said after meeting visiting Turkmen Oil, Gas Industry and Mineral Resources Minister Gochmurad Nazdzhanov in Ankara.

Iran and Turkey agreed earlier this month to build the initial parts of the pipeline on their territories. The total length of the line will be 1,420 km (890-mile) in total from Iran's Tabriz to the Turkish capital Ankara.
Iran said it would also tender for the 270-km (169-mile) part of the pipeline separately towards the end of November.
The construction of the initial sections of the line on the Iranian and Turkish territories will begin in March, 1997.

Turkey signed an agreement with its gas-rich eastern neighbour in August to get gas under a 23-year, $23-billion deal. Turkey will begin receiving three billion cubic metres (bcm) from 1998. The amount will rise to 10 bcm from 2005.

Turkey will later hold another tender after the Iranian gas reaches Erzurum, a small city in th east, to carry it to Ankara on a 800-km (500-mile) line whose capacity will be determined after talks for an additional annual 16 billion cubic metres of Russian gas through its eastern border have been finalised.
Kutan also said Turkey and Turkmenistan had agreed in principal to cooperate further on energy trade.
"We have agreed to transport Turkmen natural gas and oil through Turkey to Europe. The Iranian gas pipeline will be part of this," he said. He did not give other details.
